findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n -i "improv.*transcription|transcription quality|higher accuracy|accurate transcription" D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex` and compare each match with `CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do:116-130`. Confirm that no script or exhibit evaluates machine output against an adjudicated ground truth of transcribed names.
findings.suggested_fix: Consistently describe the paper's demonstrated empirical results as improved census linkage outcomes, middle-initial consistency, and agreement with commercial transcriptions. Soften or qualify claims in the Abstract, Introduction, and Conclusion from 'improving name transcription' and 'improving transcription quality' to 'improving census linkage outcomes through machine learning transcription' until the profile-name validation described in Section 3.3 is completed.
findings.title: The paper claims improved transcription quality although the code measures only agreement and linkage outcomes
findings.what_the_code_does: `CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do:116-130` evaluates machine transcriptions strictly by exact agreement with commercial transcriptions: Ancestry (`namefrst==namefrst_ml & namelast==namelast_ml_ditto`) and FamilySearch (`fs_namefrst==namefrst_ml & fs_namelast==namelast_ml_ditto`). It does not compare machine output against any verified or adjudicated name ground truth. While Section 2.3 (lines 278-282, 302-304), Section 1 (lines 104-106), and Section 3.3 (lines 648-652) correctly acknowledge that agreement with commercial transcribers is resemblance rather than reliability, that link validation evaluates links rather than names, and that name validation against genealogical profiles is uncompleted, the Abstract (lines 66, 71), Introduction (lines 90, 121, 131-133), and Conclusion (lines 750, 765) repeatedly claim that the method 'improves name transcription', 'improve[s] handwriting recognition', 'systematically improve[s] transcription quality', and achieves 'dramatic improvements' in data construction.
findings.why_it_matters: The central headline of the paper is improving transcription quality. But agreement with commercial transcriptions or increased downstream linkage does not prove that transcription accuracy or quality improved. If the model simply learns FamilySearch's spelling or ditto conventions, agreement and downstream matches rise without accuracy necessarily improving. A referee will challenge claims of improved transcription accuracy where only agreement and linkage are demonstrated.

findings.how_to_check: Run `git grep "97.38"` or search `CODE/` for test set evaluation scripts; confirm that no script produces the values in Table 1 or exports `tab:transcription-performance`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the evaluation script and test predictions under `CODE/` (e.g., a Python evaluation script) that loads the test set split, computes sequence and token accuracy, and outputs Table 1 directly to LaTeX.
findings.title: Out-of-sample model performance percentages in Table 1 and Appendix A.4 have no producing code in the repository
findings.what_the_code_does: Table 1 (line 261) and Appendix A.4 (line 919) report out-of-sample model performance on the test set: First name whole name 97.38%, characters 98.61%; Last name whole name 94.54%, characters 98.29%. In `CODE/`, `clean_FS_and_combineV5_nber.do:225` creates a labeled dataset (`census1940_all_labeled_data.dta`), but there is no Python or Stata code implementing the 10% test split, neural network inference, sequence accuracy evaluation, character token accuracy denominator calculations, or the generation of Table 1.
findings.why_it_matters: Under checklist `claims-vs-code.md`, every statistic in a table must be traceable to the code that produces it. Table 1 contains the manuscript's only direct empirical evaluation of the neural network's transcription performance. Without the code, reviewers cannot audit the test split, character set definitions, padding handling, or metric computations.

findings.suggested_fix: Provide the linking scripts and documentation that construct `link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and `link1930_1940_true_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` from census microdata, and archive the pipeline scripts producing the `deaglan_results` tables in the repository.
findings.title: The repository does not contain code generating the headline link files or the external robustness tables
findings.what_the_code_does: The headline linking script `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do` merges precomputed link files `link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` and `link1930_1940_true_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta` (lines 65, 75) and defines links as `_merge==3 & fiveyr==1`. While the paper (lines 418-427) describes a two-stage exact-name, birth-state, ┬▒2-year age window, and uniqueness algorithm, `CODE/` contains no code implementing this algorithm from raw records. Furthermore, the four robustness and external validation tables (Tables 5ΓÇô8) comparing ABE, Jaro-Winkler, and HLINK against FamilySearch genealogical records are imported as pre-rendered LaTeX snippets from an external `deaglan_results/current/` directory without generating code in the repository.
findings.why_it_matters: The headline 119 percent increase in linkage rates (Table 4) and the cross-algorithm robustness claims (Tables 5ΓÇô8) depend entirely on link files whose generation cannot be audited within the repository. A referee or replication reviewer cannot verify whether the linking rules, age window uniqueness, or genealogical contradiction classifications match the descriptions in the paper.

findings.how_to_check: Search `CODE/` for any population representativeness weights, balance tests against the full 1940 population, or regressions of substantive outcomes. Inspect `CODE/compute_subgroup_linkage_rates.do` and `CODE/compute_race_linkage_rates.do` to verify that only subgroup means of `linked_before` and `linked_after` are calculated.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise lines 752-753 and 765 to state that machine learning transcription increases linkage rates and expands sample sizes for historically under-linked groups, while explicitly acknowledging that determining whether this reduces bias in specific downstream empirical estimates remains an open question.
findings.title: The conclusion claims reduced empirical bias although the code estimates only subgroup linkage rates
findings.what_the_code_does: The subgroup analysis in `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:265-330`, `CODE/compute_subgroup_linkage_rates.do`, and `CODE/compute_race_linkage_rates.do` computes baseline and post-improvement linkage rates for demographic groups and calculates percentage increases (`100*(a/b - 1)`). The code does not compare the joint distribution of linked samples to the census population, nor does it estimate any empirical model (e.g., intergenerational mobility, wage returns) to assess bias reduction. In fact, for race, the linkage rate rose by 6.4% for non-whites (11.0% to 11.7%) and 7.9% for whites (24.1% to 26.0%), widening the absolute white/non-white gap from 13.1 pp to 14.3 pp. Yet the Conclusion asserts that results 'reduce biases in the empirical findings derived from them' (line 752) and 'reduc[e] demographic and geographic biases' (line 765).
findings.why_it_matters: Higher linkage rates within subgroups expand sample sizes but do not demonstrate that sample selection bias or downstream parameter estimate bias has been reduced. Claiming that empirical bias is reduced without estimating representativeness or downstream models is an unsupported empirical claim that referees will reject.

findings.how_to_check: Search `CODE/` for 'manual review', 'random sample', 'illegible', or 'segmentation'. Confirm that no dataset or script documents this manual review.
findings.suggested_fix: State the exact sample size and sampling procedure in the text, provide the sampling code and anonymized review dataset in the repository, or rephrase line 308 as an informal qualitative observation during development rather than a 'manual review of a random sample.'
findings.title: The claimed random manual review of model failure cases has no sample size, selection code, rubric, or recorded results
findings.what_the_code_does: Line 308 of `DHTS-2026-10-12.tex` asserts: 'A manual review of a random sample of these cases suggests that they largely fall into two categories: (a) cases involving particularly illegible handwriting, or (b) cases resulting from incorrect segmentation.' In `CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do:128-130`, the code counts cases where the model produced incomplete output (`nom_h`, 3,375,771 records). Nothing in `CODE/` draws a random sample, records sample size, applies a coding rubric, or stores review classifications.
findings.why_it_matters: Checklist `claims-vs-code.md` requires that where hand-validated or manual samples are claimed, they must have a stated size and protocol. Without sample size, sampling seed, or recorded data, 'largely' is an informal assertion rather than an auditable empirical finding.

review_limits: External census microdata, raw page scans, intermediate .dta files, and link files reside on external paths (D:\SNU ECON Dropbox\, F:\...) and could not be dynamically executed or regenerated.

The repository lacks neural network model training code, weights, test set splits, and evaluation scripts; hence Table 1's sequence and token accuracies (97.38/98.61/94.54/98.29%) could only be verified for internal textual consistency, not recomputed from model predictions.

The linking pipeline scripts producing link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta, link1930_1940_true_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta, and the external deaglan_results package are outside CODE/; displayed numbers match the imported LaTeX fragments, but underlying record-matching code could not be audited.

Review was restricted to the active dimension claims-vs-code; correctness, replication, and identification were not systematically evaluated except where directly relevant to claims in the paper draft.

The primary remaining issue is that the text repeatedly claims improved transcription accuracy or quality in the Abstract, Introduction, and Conclusion, even though the repository only evaluates agreement and linkage outcomes without ground-truth name validation. Secondary concerns include the lack of producing code for Table 1's test set metrics, unestimated claims of empirical bias reduction in the Conclusion, and an unrecorded manual review protocol.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
